holidays.name: Chaos Never Dies Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace the unpredictable. Spilled coffee, tangled cords and surprise plot twists all count as part of the fun. Skip the color-coded planner and let things get messy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on lists of offbeat holidays.
holidays.funFact: The day sits right next to World Freedom Day on the calendar. That makes it a fitting date for a little rule-breaking.

holidays.name: National Scrapple Day
holidays.description: A tribute to scrapple, the crispy-edged breakfast loaf. Cooks make it from pork scraps and cornmeal, then slice it and fry it until golden. Fans say it's the best part of a Mid-Atlantic breakfast.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a dish tied to Pennsylvania Dutch kitchens.
holidays.funFact: Scrapple grew out of a waste-not tradition. Early cooks used up the leftover bits from hog butchering so nothing was thrown away.

holidays.name: Geriatric Tooth Fairy Day
holidays.description: A playful day that imagines the tooth fairy visiting grown-ups. Dentures, crowns and lost molars all get their moment. Treat yourself to a little reward for surviving another year of dental appointments.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a lighthearted twist on the childhood tooth fairy tradition.
holidays.funFact: The tooth fairy has no single official origin story. Her legend blends old customs of burying or trading lost baby teeth.
